p: The video presents an opening text hook 'Humans point, agents edit.', followed by a split screen showing a document where a user leaves an inline comment to shorten a title. Below, a terminal runs a Claude agent command that reads the comment and updates the artifact, resolving the feedback in place before closing on an end card.
Artifact Share lets teammates leave inline feedback on shared AI artifacts, which AI agents can directly read and update at the same URL.

[{"timestamp":"00:00","observation":"Title card introduces the hook 'Humans point, agents edit.'"},{"timestamp":"00:06","observation":"Teammate selects the document heading and enters inline critique."},{"timestamp":"00:14","observation":"Terminal agent command executes to process the feedback."},{"timestamp":"00:19","observation":"Document updates automatically to reflect shortened text, showing resolved status."},{"timestamp":"00:26","observation":"End screen displays final CTA and product URL."}]

The video clearly communicates the core value proposition of human-in-the-loop agent edits on a single URL. Screen recordings and typography are clean and legible throughout. The runtime is significantly longer than five seconds, and pacing could be tightened to improve viewer engagement.

p: ["opening frame is a dense text slide, not a scroll-stopping visual hook","no explicit CTA or artifactshare.com URL visible in sampled frames","terminal command overlay ('claude -p ... --dangerously-skip-permissions') may read as niche/technical friction rather than reassurance"]

The screen-recording format clearly demonstrates the actual product loop — comment on a doc, agent reads it via CLI, edits, republishes at the same link — which lands the 'humans point, agents edit / same URL' message with unusual precision for the target dev audience. However the opening frame is static, text-dense, and low-contrast rather than an attention grab, so the hook is weak for a scrolling feed. No frame in the sample shows a clear call-to-action or the product URL/brand mark, leaving click intent to inference rather than an explicit prompt. Visual execution is clean and glitch-free throughout, with legible UI and terminal text.
